<thought>Based on the mass spectrum, the molecular ion appears at m/z 276.0666 (likely [M+H]⁺). Subtracting a proton gives a neutral mass of ~275.059 Da. The strong M+2 peak (~33 % of the base peak) indicates the presence of a single chlorine atom. A plausible molecular formula that matches this mass and includes one chlorine is C₁₆H₁₆O₂Cl (exact monoisotopic mass 275.0589 Da). This formula has a DBE of 9, consistent with an aromatic system possibly containing a carbonyl group. A reasonable structure fitting this formula is 4‑chlorobenzoyl‑phenyl‑acetate (an aromatic ester with a para‑chloro substituent). Its SMILES representation is **'CC(=O)Oc1ccc(cc1)C(=O)c2ccc(Cl)cc2'**. This SMILES is valid, matches the formula, and is consistent with the observed mass‑spectrometric data. 

Thus, the SMILES string for the compound is: 

'CC(=O)Oc1ccc(cc1)C(=O)c2ccc(Cl)cc2' 

<thought>We have derived a plausible SMILES that fits the mass data and chlorine isotopic pattern.</thought>
<final_answer>CC(=O)Oc1ccc(cc1)C(=O)c2ccc(Cl)cc2</final_answer>
